rows: Read every item from a paginated REST API, one page per batch

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Read all items from a paginated JSON REST API at `base_url` and return them as rows `(id, name, category, price)`. Pages are requested `page_size` at a time (named argument, default 100) and streamed to DuckDB as they arrive. If a DuckDB secret of type `terrain_api` exists its `token` is sent as a bearer token; otherwise the `TERRAIN_API_TOKEN` environment variable is used. Rate-limit (429) and server errors are retried with backoff.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## fetch_items(base_url, page_size := 100)

Every item from a paginated REST API, streamed one page per batch.

Authenticate with a `terrain_api` secret or the `TERRAIN_API_TOKEN` environment variable:

```sql
CREATE SECRET (TYPE terrain_api, TOKEN 'your-token');
```
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The five priciest hardware items from the public demo API", "sql": "SELECT id, name, price FROM terrain.examples.fetch_items('https://vgi-starter-api.query-farm.services/v1') WHERE category = 'hardware' ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5"}, {"description": "Summarize the API's items by category, ten per request", "sql": "SELECT category, count(*) AS items, avg(price) AS avg_price FROM terrain.examples.fetch_items('https://vgi-starter-api.query-farm.services/v1', page_size := 10) GROUP BY category ORDER BY category"}]

rows: Generate count rows of (n, squared), stepping n by step

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Generate a deterministic table of `count` rows with columns `n` and `squared`, where `n` runs `0, step, 2*step, ...`. `count` is positional (0 to 1,000,000); `step` is a named argument that defaults to 1, for example `sequence_table(5, step := 2)`. Rows stream back in batches, so large counts do not buffer in memory.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## sequence_table(count, step := 1)

`count` rows of `(n, squared)` with `n = 0, step, 2*step, ...`.

Deterministic, so it is handy for tests and demos.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The first five values and their squares", "sql": "SELECT n, squared FROM terrain.examples.sequence_table(5) ORDER BY n"}, {"description": "Four values stepping by ten", "sql": "SELECT n FROM terrain.examples.sequence_table(4, step := 10) ORDER BY n"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Three rows stepping by two", "sql": "SELECT n, squared FROM terrain.examples.sequence_table(3, step := 2) ORDER BY n", "expected_result": [[0, 0], [2, 4], [4, 16]]}, {"description": "Count the rows generated", "sql": "SELECT count(*) AS rows FROM terrain.examples.sequence_table(1000)", "expected_result": [[1000]]}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "n", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "The generated value: row index times step."}, {"name": "squared", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "n multiplied by itself."}]

Read DEM cell centres, elevation, slope and aspect

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Read north-up projected metre DEM cells as rows. Nodata becomes NULL; finite-difference slope and aspect are NULL where neighbours are missing. Flat cells have NULL aspect. Cross join cells to observer locations and pass the endpoint pairs to visibility for a sampled viewshed. max_cells bounds memory. Elevations must be metres.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## DEM cells and surfaces

Read north-up projected metre DEM cells as rows. Nodata becomes NULL; finite-difference slope and aspect are NULL where neighbours are missing. Flat cells have NULL aspect. Cross join cells to observer locations and pass the endpoint pairs to visibility for a sampled viewshed. max_cells bounds memory. Elevations must be metres.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Count cells and find the ridge elevation", "sql": "SELECT count(*), max(elevation_m) FROM terrain.main.dem_cells('demo://ridge.tif')"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "DEM cells and surfaces on bundled synthetic data", "sql": "SELECT count(*), max(elevation_m) FROM terrain.main.dem_cells('demo://ridge.tif')", "expected_result": [[121, 30.0]]}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "cell_id", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Row-major DEM cell index."}, {"name": "x", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Cell centre X in dem_crs."}, {"name": "y", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Cell centre Y in dem_crs."}, {"name": "elevation_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Elevation in metres; NULL for nodata."}, {"name": "slope_deg", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Slope from finite differences in degrees; NULL where neighbouring data are missing."}, {"name": "aspect_deg", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Downhill azimuth clockwise from north; NULL on flat or unknown terrain."}, {"name": "dem_crs", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Projected horizontal CRS, with metre units."}]

Assess terrain obstruction between tower and building pairs

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Evaluate terrain visibility between query-supplied tower/building pairs and inspect DEM elevation, slope and aspect. Distances and heights are metres. Input coordinates have an explicit CRS; DEMs must be projected in metres. Missing terrain yields unknown visibility. Synthetic demo assets ship in the wheel. The main schema exposes demo_input, visibility and dem_cells; the examples schema retains SDK regression recipes. Heights are above the DEM surface. This is sampled terrain visibility, not a radio propagation model. Nodata produces NULL visible; invalid inputs fail.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## Terrain visibility

Evaluate terrain visibility between query-supplied tower/building pairs and inspect DEM elevation, slope and aspect. Distances and heights are metres. Input coordinates have an explicit CRS; DEMs must be projected in metres. Missing terrain yields unknown visibility. Synthetic demo assets ship in the wheel. The main schema exposes demo_input, visibility and dem_cells; the examples schema retains SDK regression recipes. Heights are above the DEM surface. This is sampled terrain visibility, not a radio propagation model. Nodata produces NULL visible; invalid inputs fail.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "A tall tower clears the ridge; a low tower is blocked", "sql": "SELECT pair_id, visible, status FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT * FROM terrain.main.demo_input)) ORDER BY pair_id"}, {"description": "Viewshed per tower: cross join each demo_input tower with every dem_cells cell centre, run visibility on the 242 sight lines, and count visible vs blocked cells (80 m tower 99/22, 2 m tower 55/66 of 121)", "sql": "SELECT split_part(v.pair_id, ':', 1) AS tower, count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.visible) AS visible_cells, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT v.visible) AS blocked_cells FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT t.pair_id || ':' || c.cell_id AS pair_id, t.source_x, t.source_y, c.x AS target_x, c.y AS target_y, t.source_height_m, 2.0 AS target_height_m FROM terrain.main.demo_input AS t CROSS JOIN terrain.main.dem_cells('demo://ridge.tif') AS c)) AS v GROUP BY tower ORDER BY tower"}, {"description": "Locate what blocks each blocked pair: snap the visibility obstruction point to the nearest dem_cells cell centre (the 2 m tower's line passes 28 m under the 30 m ridge crest cell 60)", "sql": "SELECT v.pair_id, round(v.min_clearance_m, 2) AS min_clearance_m, c.cell_id, c.x, c.y, c.elevation_m FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT * FROM terrain.main.demo_input)) AS v CROSS JOIN terrain.main.dem_cells('demo://ridge.tif') AS c WHERE v.status = 'blocked' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY v.pair_id ORDER BY (c.x - v.obstruction_x) ^ 2 + (c.y - v.obstruction_y) ^ 2, c.cell_id) = 1 ORDER BY v.pair_id"}, {"description": "Tower height sweep: re-run the demo_input 'low' pair through visibility at heights 40-70 m in 5 m steps; heights up to 55 m are blocked by the ridge and 60 m is the first that clears it (+1.0 m)", "sql": "WITH candidates AS (SELECT 'low@' || h.height_m AS pair_id, h.height_m, d.source_x, d.source_y, d.target_x, d.target_y, h.height_m::DOUBLE AS source_height_m, d.target_height_m FROM terrain.main.demo_input AS d CROSS JOIN range(40, 75, 5) AS h(height_m) WHERE d.pair_id = 'low') SELECT c.height_m, v.status, round(v.min_clearance_m, 2) AS min_clearance_m FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT * FROM candidates)) AS v JOIN candidates AS c USING (pair_id) ORDER BY c.height_m"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Terrain visibility on bundled synthetic data", "sql": "SELECT pair_id, visible, status FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT * FROM terrain.main.demo_input)) ORDER BY pair_id", "expected_result": [["high", true, "visible"], ["low", false, "blocked"]]}, {"description": "Viewshed per tower: cross join each demo_input tower with every dem_cells cell centre, run visibility on the 242 sight lines, and count visible vs blocked cells (80 m tower 99/22, 2 m tower 55/66 of 121)", "sql": "SELECT split_part(v.pair_id, ':', 1) AS tower, count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.visible) AS visible_cells, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT v.visible) AS blocked_cells FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT t.pair_id || ':' || c.cell_id AS pair_id, t.source_x, t.source_y, c.x AS target_x, c.y AS target_y, t.source_height_m, 2.0 AS target_height_m FROM terrain.main.demo_input AS t CROSS JOIN terrain.main.dem_cells('demo://ridge.tif') AS c)) AS v GROUP BY tower ORDER BY tower", "expected_result": [["high", 99, 22], ["low", 55, 66]]}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "pair_id", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Input pair identity, suitable for joining to towers and buildings."}, {"name": "visible", "type": "BOOLEAN", "description": "True if all sampled terrain clears the sight line; NULL if coverage is unknown."}, {"name": "distance_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Horizontal distance in the projected DEM CRS, metres."}, {"name": "min_clearance_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Smallest interior sight-line clearance above terrain, metres."}, {"name": "obstruction_x", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Worst obstruction X in dem_crs, only when blocked."}, {"name": "obstruction_y", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Worst obstruction Y in dem_crs, only when blocked."}, {"name": "sample_count", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Number of elevation samples used along this sight line."}, {"name": "status", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "visible, blocked, outside_dem, or nodata; unknown terrain is never reported clear."}, {"name": "sightline_wkb", "type": "BLOB", "description": "3D WKB sight line with absolute endpoint elevations; NULL without terrain coverage."}, {"name": "dem_crs", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Horizontal coordinate reference system of the output geometry and obstruction."}]
rows.vgi.title: Terrain visibility

rows: SELECT pair_id, visible, status FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT * FROM terrain.main.demo_input)) ORDER BY pair_id

SELECT split_part(v.pair_id, ':', 1) AS tower, count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.visible) AS visible_cells, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT v.visible) AS blocked_cells FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT t.pair_id || ':' || c.cell_id AS pair_id, t.source_x, t.source_y, c.x AS target_x, c.y AS target_y, t.source_height_m, 2.0 AS target_height_m FROM terrain.main.demo_input AS t CROSS JOIN terrain.main.dem_cells('demo://ridge.tif') AS c)) AS v GROUP BY tower ORDER BY tower

SELECT v.pair_id, round(v.min_clearance_m, 2) AS min_clearance_m, c.cell_id, c.x, c.y, c.elevation_m FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT * FROM terrain.main.demo_input)) AS v CROSS JOIN terrain.main.dem_cells('demo://ridge.tif') AS c WHERE v.status = 'blocked' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY v.pair_id ORDER BY (c.x - v.obstruction_x) ^ 2 + (c.y - v.obstruction_y) ^ 2, c.cell_id) = 1 ORDER BY v.pair_id

WITH candidates AS (SELECT 'low@' || h.height_m AS pair_id, h.height_m, d.source_x, d.source_y, d.target_x, d.target_y, h.height_m::DOUBLE AS source_height_m, d.target_height_m FROM terrain.main.demo_input AS d CROSS JOIN range(40, 75, 5) AS h(height_m) WHERE d.pair_id = 'low') SELECT c.height_m, v.status, round(v.min_clearance_m, 2) AS min_clearance_m FROM terrain.main.visibility((SELECT * FROM candidates)) AS v JOIN candidates AS c USING (pair_id) ORDER BY c.height_m
